message: Login to the AWS Console. Choose your account name on the top right of the window -> My Account -> Contact Information.
status_detail: Login to the AWS Console. Choose your account name on the top right of the window -> My Account -> Contact Information.

AWS-Account-Security-Onboarding: Billing, emergency, security contacts

analytic.name: AWS account contact information is current

finding_info.desc: **AWS account contact information** is current for the **primary contact** and the **alternate contacts** for `security`, `billing`, and `operations`, with accurate email addresses and phone numbers.
finding_info.title: AWS account contact information is current
types: Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices

remediation.desc:
Adopt:
- **Primary** and **alternate contacts** for `security`, `billing`, `operations`
- Shared, monitored aliases and SMS-capable phone numbers (non-personal)
- Centralized management across accounts with periodic reviews
- **Least privilege** for who can modify contact data
- Regular reachability tests and documented ownership

risk_details:
Outdated or single-person contacts delay **security notifications**, slow **incident response**, and complicate **account recovery**.

AWS may throttle services during abuse mitigation, reducing **availability**. Missed alerts enable ongoing misuse, risking **data exfiltration** and unauthorized changes (**integrity**).

message: SECURITY, BILLING and OPERATIONS contacts not found or they are not different between each other and between ROOT contact.
status_detail: SECURITY, BILLING and OPERATIONS contacts not found or they are not different between each other and between ROOT contact.

analytic.name: AWS account has distinct Security, Billing, and Operations contact details, different from each other and from the root contact

finding_info.desc: **AWS account alternate contacts** are defined for **Security**, **Billing**, and **Operations** with `name`, `email`, and `phone`. The finding evaluates that all three exist, are distinct from one another, and differ from the **primary (root) contact**.
finding_info.title: AWS account has distinct Security, Billing, and Operations contact details, different from each other and from the root contact
types: Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark

remediation.desc:
Maintain distinct, monitored **Security**, **Billing**, and **Operations** alternate contacts that differ from the root contact.
- Use team aliases and 24x7 phones
- Review and test contact paths regularly
- Centralize at org level for consistency

Applies **operational resilience** and **separation of duties**.

risk_details: Missing or shared contacts can delay response to abuse alerts, credential compromise, or billing anomalies, reducing **availability** (possible AWS traffic throttling) and raising **confidentiality** and **integrity** risk through extended exposure. If AWS cannot reach you, urgent mitigation may disrupt service.

message: Login to the AWS Console. Choose your account name on the top right of the window -> My Account -> Alternate Contacts -> Security Section.
status_detail: Login to the AWS Console. Choose your account name on the top right of the window -> My Account -> Alternate Contacts -> Security Section.

AWS-Account-Security-Onboarding: Billing, emergency, security contacts

analytic.name: AWS account has security alternate contact registered

finding_info.desc: Account settings contain a **Security alternate contact** in Alternate Contacts (name, `EmailAddress`, `PhoneNumber`) for targeted AWS security notifications.
finding_info.title: AWS account has security alternate contact registered
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices

remediation.desc:
Define and maintain a **Security alternate contact**:
- Use a monitored alias (e.g., `security@domain`) and team phone
- Apply to every account (prefer Org-wide automation)
- Review after org/personnel changes and test delivery
- Document ownership and escalation paths
Align with **incident response** and **least privilege** principles.

risk_details:
Missing or outdated **security contact** can delay or prevent AWS advisories from reaching responders, increasing risk to:
- Confidentiality: data exfiltration from undetected compromise
- Integrity: unauthorized changes persist longer
- Availability: resource abuse (e.g., cryptomining) and outages

message: Login to the AWS Console as root. Choose your account name on the top right of the window -> My Account -> Configure Security Challenge Questions.
status_detail: Login to the AWS Console as root. Choose your account name on the top right of the window -> My Account -> Configure Security Challenge Questions.

analytic.name: [DEPRECATED] AWS root user has security challenge questions configured

finding_info.desc: [DEPRECATED] **AWS account root** configuration may include legacy **security challenge questions** for support identity verification. This evaluates whether those questions are set on the account. *New configuration is discontinued by AWS and remaining support for this feature is time-limited.*
finding_info.title: [DEPRECATED] AWS root user has security challenge questions configured
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices

remediation.desc:
Favor stronger recovery instead of KBA:
- Enforce **MFA for root** and minimize root use
- Keep **alternate contacts** and root email current and protected
- Establish a tightly controlled **break-glass role**, applying least privilege and separation of duties
- Document and test recovery procedures; monitor root activity

risk_details: Absence of these questions can limit support-assisted recovery if root credentials or MFA are lost, reducing **availability** and slowing **incident response**. Reliance on KBA also weakens **confidentiality** due to **social engineering**. Treat this as a recovery gap and adopt stronger, phishing-resistant factors.

message: At least one Backup Plan exists: aws/efs/automatic-backup-plan.
status_detail: At least one Backup Plan exists: aws/efs/automatic-backup-plan.

analytic.name: At least one AWS Backup plan exists

finding_info.desc:
**AWS Backup** is assessed for the existence of at least one **backup plan** that schedules and retains recovery points for selected resources.

The evaluation determines whether any plan is configured; when none is found-even if backup vaults exist-the absence of a plan is noted.
finding_info.title: At least one AWS Backup plan exists
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices

remediation.desc:
Establish and enforce **backup plans** for critical workloads:
- Define schedules, retention, and lifecycle to meet RPO/RTO
- Use tagging to include all required resources by policy
- Enable cross-Region/account copies and immutability where feasible
- Apply least privilege to backup roles
- Regularly test restores and review reports

risk_details:
Without a backup plan, resources lack scheduled recovery points, undermining RPO/RTO.
- Irrecoverable data after deletion or corruption (integrity)
- Prolonged outages due to unavailable restores (availability)
- Inconsistent backups that hinder investigations and controlled recovery

message: No Backup Report Plan exist.
status_detail: No Backup Report Plan exist.

analytic.name: At least one AWS Backup report plan exists

finding_info.desc: **AWS Backup** environments with existing backup plans are assessed for the presence of at least one **report plan** that generates `jobs` or `compliance` reports.
finding_info.title: At least one AWS Backup report plan exists
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices

remediation.desc:
Establish and maintain **report plans** to continuously monitor backup activity and policy adherence.
- Apply least privilege to report storage
- Include relevant accounts and Regions for coverage
- Review reports routinely and alert on anomalies
- Enforce separation of duties between backup admins and auditors

risk_details: Without a report plan, backup failures and missed restores may go unnoticed, harming **availability** and recovery objectives. Gaps in retention, scheduling, or encryption controls can persist unreported, weakening **integrity** and auditability across accounts and Regions, increasing the chance of SLA breaches.

message: Backup Vault aws/efs/automatic-backup-vault is encrypted at rest.
status_detail: Backup Vault aws/efs/automatic-backup-vault is encrypted at rest.

analytic.name: AWS Backup vault is encrypted at rest

finding_info.desc: **AWS Backup vaults** are evaluated for **encryption at rest** with **AWS KMS**. The finding highlights vaults without a configured KMS key protecting stored recovery points.
finding_info.title: AWS Backup vault is encrypted at rest
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/NIST 800-53 Controls (USA)
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/NIST CSF Controls (USA)
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/PCI-DSS
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/ISO 27001 Controls
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/HIPAA Controls (USA)

remediation.desc: Encrypt every backup vault with **customer-managed KMS keys** (`CMK`). Enforce **least privilege** in key policies, enable rotation, and separate key admins from backup operators. Add **defense-in-depth** with vault lock and logging. *For copies*, ensure destination vaults use appropriate KMS keys.

risk_details: Unencrypted vaults allow recovery points to be read if storage or credentials are compromised, undermining **confidentiality** and enabling data exfiltration. Missing KMS controls also weaken **integrity** guarantees and impede forensic **auditability** during investigations.

message: At least one backup vault exists: aws/efs/automatic-backup-vault.
status_detail: At least one backup vault exists: aws/efs/automatic-backup-vault.

analytic.name: At least one AWS Backup vault exists

finding_info.desc: **AWS Backup** in the account/region includes at least one **backup vault** that stores and organizes recovery points for use by backup plans and copies.
finding_info.title: At least one AWS Backup vault exists
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices

remediation.desc: Create and maintain a **backup vault** in each required region. Enforce **least privilege** access, encrypt with **KMS CMKs**, and enable **Vault Lock** to prevent tampering. Use lifecycle rules and cross-region/cross-account copies, and regularly test restores for **defense in depth**.

risk_details: Without a vault, recovery points cannot be created or retained in AWS Backup, degrading **availability** and **integrity**. Data may be irrecoverable after deletion, ransomware, or misconfiguration, and RPO/RTO targets may be missed during incidents.

message: Backup Vault aws/efs/automatic-backup-vault does not have Vault Lock enabled.
status_detail: Backup Vault aws/efs/automatic-backup-vault does not have Vault Lock enabled.

unmapped.notes: `Locked=true` is reported for both governance and compliance mode; the ListBackupVaults response does not distinguish them, so this check does not assert which mode is in use. Compliance mode becomes immutable once the cooling-off period set by ChangeableForDays expires and cannot be removed afterwards, including by the account root user.

analytic.name: AWS Backup vault has Vault Lock enabled

finding_info.desc: **AWS Backup vaults** are evaluated for **Vault Lock** (`Locked=true`), which enforces a write-once-read-many (WORM) retention policy on the recovery points the vault holds.
finding_info.title: AWS Backup vault has Vault Lock enabled
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Effects/Data Destruction

remediation.desc:
Enable **Vault Lock** on backup vaults so recovery points cannot be deleted or have their retention shortened before the configured period elapses.

Use **governance mode** where privileged users must retain the ability to remove the lock, and **compliance mode** where immutability is a regulatory requirement. Note that compliance mode cannot be undone once the cooling-off period expires, so validate the retention window first.

risk_details:
Without **Vault Lock**, backups in the vault can be **deleted or have their retention shortened** by anyone with sufficient permissions.

That removes the last line of defence against **ransomware** and accidental deletion: an attacker with a privileged principal can destroy recovery points before encrypting production data, defeating the recovery plan.

message: Bedrock custom models could not be listed in region ap-northeast-2 (UnknownOperationException); verify manually that every custom model uses a customer-managed KMS key.
status_detail: Bedrock custom models could not be listed in region ap-northeast-2 (UnknownOperationException); verify manually that every custom model uses a customer-managed KMS key.

unmapped.notes: Reports one finding per custom model, reading modelKmsKeyArn from GetCustomModel because ListCustomModels summaries do not carry it. A model whose detail could not be retrieved returns MANUAL rather than PASS, because an absent key ARN means the answer is unknown, not that no key is set.

analytic.name: Bedrock custom model is encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key

finding_info.desc: **Bedrock custom models** produced by model customization can be encrypted at rest with a customer-managed KMS key rather than resting under an AWS-owned key the organization cannot audit, rotate, or revoke.
finding_info.title: Bedrock custom model is encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Data Encryption

remediation.desc: Choose a customer-managed KMS key when creating each model customization job so the resulting custom model rests under a key with an auditable policy and rotation. The key cannot be changed after the model is created, so re-run customization for existing models.

risk_details:
A **fine-tuned model** is derived from the training data used to build it and can leak that data through inference.

Under an **AWS-owned key**, the organization has no key policy to restrict who may decrypt the artifacts, no customer-controlled rotation, no **CloudTrail** record of key usage, and no way to revoke access to the model by disabling a key.

message: IAM Role gridguard-aws-sandbox-foundation-deploy does not have AmazonBedrockFullAccess policy attached.
status_detail: IAM Role gridguard-aws-sandbox-foundation-deploy does not have AmazonBedrockFullAccess policy attached.

analytic.name: IAM role does not have AmazonBedrockFullAccess managed policy attached

finding_info.desc:
**IAM roles** (excluding service roles) are evaluated for attachment of the AWS-managed `AmazonBedrockFullAccess` policy.

This policy grants unrestricted access to all Amazon Bedrock actions and resources.
finding_info.title: IAM role does not have AmazonBedrockFullAccess managed policy attached
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices

remediation.desc:
Apply **least privilege**: replace `AmazonBedrockFullAccess` with a custom policy granting only the specific Bedrock actions required.

Use **permissions boundaries** and **SCPs** to limit the scope of Bedrock permissions. Regularly review access with **IAM Access Analyzer** to identify and remove unused privileges.

risk_details:
The `AmazonBedrockFullAccess` policy grants broad permissions across all Bedrock resources. If a role with this policy is compromised, an attacker could:
- Invoke any model to exfiltrate data or generate harmful content
- Modify guardrails, logging, and security configurations
- Incur significant costs through unrestricted model invocations

message: Bedrock has no guardrails configured in region ap-northeast-1.
status_detail: Bedrock has no guardrails configured in region ap-northeast-1.

unmapped.notes: This check validates guardrail existence per successfully scanned region. It does not verify attachment to agents or the use of guardrails on model invocations. Regions where Bedrock guardrails cannot be enumerated are skipped to avoid false failures.

analytic.name: Bedrock has at least one guardrail configured in the audited region

finding_info.desc:
**Amazon Bedrock guardrails** provide reusable safety policies for filtering harmful or unwanted content in model inputs and outputs.

This evaluation checks whether at least one guardrail exists in each successfully scanned region. It does **not** verify that guardrails are attached to agents or passed on individual model invocation API calls.
finding_info.title: Bedrock has at least one guardrail configured in the audited region
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Runtime Behavior Analysis

remediation.desc:
Create at least one **Bedrock guardrail** in each region where Bedrock is used, then separately ensure those guardrails are attached to relevant agents and invocation paths.
- Configure **content filters** for harmful categories (hate, violence, sexual, misconduct)
- Add **sensitive information filters** and **denied topic policies**
- Apply guardrails at the API call level using `guardrailIdentifier` where supported

risk_details: Without any configured **Bedrock guardrails** in a region, teams lack a native reusable policy object for **content filtering** and **safety controls**. Applications may invoke models without standardized protections against **harmful content**, **prompt injection**, or **sensitive-data exposure** unless equivalent controls are enforced elsewhere.

**Amazon Bedrock guardrails** provide reusable safety policies for filtering harmful or unwanted content in model inputs and outputs.

This evaluation checks whether at least one guardrail exists in each successfully scanned region. It does **not** verify that guardrails are attached to agents or passed on individual model invocation API calls.
finding_info.title: Bedrock has at least one guardrail configured in the audited region
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Runtime Behavior Analysis

remediation.desc:
Create at least one **Bedrock guardrail** in each region where Bedrock is used, then separately ensure those guardrails are attached to relevant agents and invocation paths.
- Configure **content filters** for harmful categories (hate, violence, sexual, misconduct)
- Add **sensitive information filters** and **denied topic policies**
- Apply guardrails at the API call level using `guardrailIdentifier` where supported

risk_details: Without any configured **Bedrock guardrails** in a region, teams lack a native reusable policy object for **content filtering** and **safety controls**. Applications may invoke models without standardized protections against **harmful content**, **prompt injection**, or **sensitive-data exposure** unless equivalent controls are enforced elsewhere.

finding_info.title: Amazon Bedrock model invocation logging is enabled
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices

remediation.desc:
Enable **model invocation logging** and route events to **CloudWatch Logs** and/or **S3**.

Enforce **least privilege** on log access, use encryption, and set retention/lifecycle policies. Monitor for anomalies and alerts to support **defense in depth** and **separation of duties**.

analytic.name: Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management prompts exist in the region

finding_info.desc:
**Bedrock Prompt Management** enables centralized creation, versioning, and governance of prompts used with foundation models.

This region-level check verifies whether at least one managed prompt exists in each scanned region, used as an adoption signal for Prompt Management. The presence of a prompt does not by itself guarantee that every application prompt is managed.
finding_info.title: Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management prompts exist in the region
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices

remediation.desc:
Adopt **Bedrock Prompt Management** to centralize prompt definitions, enforce versioning, and maintain governance over model interactions.

Use managed prompts with **guardrails** and apply **least privilege** access controls to restrict who can create or modify prompts.

risk_details:
Without **Prompt Management**, prompts are scattered across applications with no central oversight, versioning, or auditability over instructions sent to foundation models, weakening governance and compliance posture.

Managed prompts are a governance enabler; **prompt injection** defenses are provided by Bedrock **guardrails**, covered by separate checks.

unmapped.notes: Results are generated per scanned region. Regions where `ListPrompts` cannot be queried are omitted from the findings.

analytic.name: Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management prompts exist in the region

finding_info.desc:
**Bedrock Prompt Management** enables centralized creation, versioning, and governance of prompts used with foundation models.

This region-level check verifies whether at least one managed prompt exists in each scanned region, used as an adoption signal for Prompt Management. The presence of a prompt does not by itself guarantee that every application prompt is managed.
finding_info.title: Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management prompts exist in the region
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices

remediation.desc:
Adopt **Bedrock Prompt Management** to centralize prompt definitions, enforce versioning, and maintain governance over model interactions.

Use managed prompts with **guardrails** and apply **least privilege** access controls to restrict who can create or modify prompts.

risk_details:
Without **Prompt Management**, prompts are scattered across applications with no central oversight, versioning, or auditability over instructions sent to foundation models, weakening governance and compliance posture.

Managed prompts are a governance enabler; **prompt injection** defenses are provided by Bedrock **guardrails**, covered by separate checks.

message: IAM Role gridguard-aws-sandbox-foundation-deploy does not have BedrockAgentCoreFullAccess or AgentRegistryFullAccess policy attached.
status_detail: IAM Role gridguard-aws-sandbox-foundation-deploy does not have BedrockAgentCoreFullAccess or AgentRegistryFullAccess policy attached.

analytic.name: IAM role does not have the AWS-managed Bedrock AgentCore full access policies attached

finding_info.desc:
**IAM roles** (excluding service roles) are evaluated for attachment of the AWS-managed `BedrockAgentCoreFullAccess` or `AgentRegistryFullAccess` policies.

These policies grant unrestricted access to the `bedrock-agentcore` and `agent-registry` actions respectively.
finding_info.title: IAM role does not have the AWS-managed Bedrock AgentCore full access policies attached
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
TTPs/Privilege Escalation

remediation.desc: Apply **least privilege**: replace `BedrockAgentCoreFullAccess` and `AgentRegistryFullAccess` with custom policies granting only the specific actions a workload calls, scoped to specific resource ARNs. Keep the control-plane actions that reconfigure gateways and policy engines separate from the invoke actions agents need at runtime.

risk_details:
**Full AgentCore access** is not only the ability to invoke agents. It includes `UpdateGateway`, `PutResourcePolicy` and the policy-engine calls.

So one compromised credential can disable a gateway authorizer, flip a policy engine to `LOG_ONLY`, or grant itself cross-account access, and then invoke the agent it just unguarded.

message: No secrets found in CloudFormation Stack gridguard-eks-lab-deployment-policy Outputs.
status_detail: No secrets found in CloudFormation Stack gridguard-eks-lab-deployment-policy Outputs.

unmapped.notes: Infrastructure Protection

analytic.name: CloudFormation stack outputs do not contain secrets

finding_info.desc: **CloudFormation stack Outputs** are analyzed for hardcoded secrets-passwords, API keys, tokens-using pattern-based detection across output values. A finding indicates potential secret strings present within `Outputs` of the template or stack.
finding_info.title: CloudFormation stack outputs do not contain secrets
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Sensitive Data Identifications/Passwords
Sensitive Data Identifications/Security
Effects/Data Exposure

remediation.desc: Remove secrets from `Outputs`. Store credentials in **Secrets Manager** or **Parameter Store** and reference them via dynamic references; set `NoEcho` for sensitive parameters. Apply **least privilege** to view stack metadata, avoid exporting sensitive values, and add automated IaC secret scanning for **defense in depth**.

risk_details: **Secrets in Outputs** are readable to anyone with stack metadata access, enabling credential theft, unauthorized API calls, and lateral movement. Exposure via consoles, exports, or CI logs undermines confidentiality and can lead to privilege escalation and data exfiltration.

message: CloudFormation Stack gridguard-eks-lab-deployment-policy has termination protection disabled.
status_detail: CloudFormation Stack gridguard-eks-lab-deployment-policy has termination protection disabled.

unmapped.notes: Infrastructure Protection

analytic.name: CloudFormation stack has termination protection enabled

finding_info.desc: **AWS CloudFormation root stacks** are evaluated for **termination protection**. The detection identifies whether `termination protection` is enabled to block stack deletions on non-nested stacks.
finding_info.title: CloudFormation stack has termination protection enabled
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Effects/Data Destruction

remediation.desc: Enable **termination protection** on root stacks for critical workloads. Enforce **least privilege** on who can alter this setting or delete stacks, require **change review** via change sets, and apply **stack policies** plus `DeletionPolicy: Retain` for data stores for defense in depth.

risk_details:
Without **termination protection**, human error or automation can delete entire stacks, causing immediate **availability** loss and potential **data destruction** of managed resources.

Attackers with delete rights can more easily trigger outages and hinder recovery.

remediation.desc: Enable **termination protection** on root stacks for critical workloads. Enforce **least privilege** on who can alter this setting or delete stacks, require **change review** via change sets, and apply **stack policies** plus `DeletionPolicy: Retain` for data stores for defense in depth.

risk_details:
Without **termination protection**, human error or automation can delete entire stacks, causing immediate **availability** loss and potential **data destruction** of managed resources.

Attackers with delete rights can more easily trigger outages and hinder recovery.

message: Cannot evaluate Amazon Bedrock AgentCore data event logging: the AgentCore resources behind AWS::BedrockAgentCore::Memory could not be listed (bedrock-agentcore:List*).
status_detail: Cannot evaluate Amazon Bedrock AgentCore data event logging: the AgentCore resources behind AWS::BedrockAgentCore::Memory could not be listed (bedrock-agentcore:List*).

unmapped.notes: Required types come from the AgentCore inventory: memories, gateways, agent runtimes (Runtime or RuntimeEndpoint), and account-owned code interpreters and browsers. With no AgentCore resources the check reports nothing unless unused services are scanned, in which case any AgentCore type passes. Coverage is account-wide, so a single-Region trail counts for every Region. Unlike `cloudtrail_bedrock_logging_enabled`, a selector that also filters on `eventName`, `readOnly`, `resources.ARN` or any other field is reported MANUAL, not PASS, because the configuration cannot show what it leaves unlogged.

analytic.name: CloudTrail logs Amazon Bedrock AgentCore data events

finding_info.desc:
**Actively logging CloudTrail trails** select **Amazon Bedrock AgentCore data events** through advanced event selectors for every AgentCore resource type the account runs: memories, gateways, agent runtimes, and custom code interpreters and browsers.

AgentCore data events are **not logged by default** and a basic event selector cannot select them.
finding_info.title: CloudTrail logs Amazon Bedrock AgentCore data events
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices

remediation.desc: Add an **advanced event selector** with `eventCategory` `Data` for each `AWS::BedrockAgentCore::*` resource type you run, one `resources.type` per selector, on a multi-Region trail. Data events are **billed per event**, so size the trail first. Gateway records redact tool arguments and results, so pair them with AgentCore observability for the reasoning trace.

risk_details:
A trail limited to **management events** records which agents, memories and gateways exist, never who invoked them or what they returned.

An agent driven into a **confused-deputy** or exfiltration path, or a **poisoned memory**, leaves no audit trail, so a session cannot be reconstructed and detections built on invocation activity never fire.

message: Trail cloud-trail-grp01 from home region eu-west-3 has management events enabled to log Amazon Bedrock control-plane API calls.
status_detail: Trail cloud-trail-grp01 from home region eu-west-3 has management events enabled to log Amazon Bedrock control-plane API calls.

unmapped.notes: This check passes when CloudTrail captures Bedrock control-plane activity via management events or Bedrock data events via advanced selectors. It does not require multi-region coverage, and it does not by itself guarantee `InvokeModel` visibility unless Bedrock data events are selected; use `bedrock_model_invocation_logging_enabled` for model invocation logs. Additional advanced selector filters such as `eventName` or `resources.ARN` can further narrow effective coverage and should be reviewed explicitly.

analytic.name: CloudTrail logs Amazon Bedrock API calls for security auditing

finding_info.desc:
**At least one actively logging CloudTrail trail** records **Amazon Bedrock API activity** through management events or advanced event selectors targeting Bedrock resources.

This check covers **control-plane** operations such as configuration changes through CloudTrail management events and can also cover **data-plane** Bedrock events when advanced event selectors target Bedrock resource types.
finding_info.title: CloudTrail logs Amazon Bedrock API calls for security auditing
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices

remediation.desc:
Enable CloudTrail logging for Amazon Bedrock on **at least one actively logging trail**. At minimum, enable **management events** to capture Bedrock control-plane operations. For invocation-level and other data-plane visibility, add **advanced event selectors** targeting Bedrock resource types or pair this control with `bedrock_model_invocation_logging_enabled`.

For broader region coverage, pair this control with a separate multi-region CloudTrail check. Centralize logs in an encrypted bucket or CloudWatch Logs to support **defense in depth** and forensic readiness for AI workloads.

risk_details: Without CloudTrail logging for Bedrock control-plane operations, changes to prompts, guardrails, agents, flows, or knowledge bases can become invisible, weakening forensics and incident response. Management events do not capture `InvokeModel`; pair this control with `bedrock_model_invocation_logging_enabled` or Bedrock data event selectors for invocation visibility.

message: Trail cloud-trail-grp01 bucket (cloud-trail-logs-grp01) does not have MFA delete enabled.
status_detail: Trail cloud-trail-grp01 bucket (cloud-trail-logs-grp01) does not have MFA delete enabled.

analytic.name: CloudTrail trail S3 bucket has MFA delete enabled

finding_info.desc: **CloudTrail log buckets** for actively logging trails are evaluated for **MFA Delete** on the associated S3 bucket. The assessment determines whether `MFA Delete` is configured on the in-account log bucket; *if the bucket resides in another account, its configuration should be verified separately*.
finding_info.title: CloudTrail trail S3 bucket has MFA delete enabled
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark

remediation.desc: Enable `MFA Delete` on the CloudTrail log bucket with versioning enabled. Enforce **least privilege** so only tightly controlled identities can delete or alter logs, and require MFA for such actions. Apply **defense in depth** using a dedicated logging account and log file integrity validation.

risk_details: Without **MFA Delete**, stolen or over-privileged credentials can permanently delete log versions or change versioning, compromising log **integrity** and **availability**. This enables attacker cover-ups, hinders **forensics**, and weakens evidence for investigations.

message: Multiregion trail cloud-trail-grp01 has not been logging in the last 24h or is not configured to deliver logs.
status_detail: Multiregion trail cloud-trail-grp01 has not been logging in the last 24h or is not configured to deliver logs.

analytic.name: CloudTrail trail has delivered logs to CloudWatch Logs in the last 24 hours

finding_info.desc: **CloudTrail trails** are configured to send events to **CloudWatch Logs**, and show recent delivery within the last `24h`. Trails without integration or without recent CloudWatch delivery are identified, across single-Region and multi-Region trails.
finding_info.title: CloudTrail trail has delivered logs to CloudWatch Logs in the last 24 hours
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark

remediation.desc: Integrate every trail with **CloudWatch Logs** and maintain continuous, near-real-time delivery. Enforce **least privilege** on the delivery role, prefer **multi-Region** coverage, and implement **metric filters and alerts** for sensitive actions. Centralize retention to support **defense in depth**.

risk_details:
Missing or stale CloudWatch delivery weakens visibility and delays detection, impacting confidentiality and integrity. Adversaries can:
- Hide **privilege escalation**
- Perform unauthorized **resource changes**
- Exfiltrate data via API misuse

message: Trail cloud-trail-grp01 does not have insight selectors and it is logging.
status_detail: Trail cloud-trail-grp01 does not have insight selectors and it is logging.

analytic.name: CloudTrail trail has Insights enabled

finding_info.desc: **CloudTrail trails** that are logging are evaluated for **Insights** via `insight selectors`, which enable anomaly detection on management-event patterns (API call and error rates). The finding pinpoints logging trails where these selectors are missing.
finding_info.title: CloudTrail trail has Insights enabled
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Runtime Behavior Analysis
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark

remediation.desc: Enable **CloudTrail Insights** on all logging trails (ideally all-Region or organization trails). Activate both `ApiCallRateInsight` and `ApiErrorRateInsight`. Integrate alerts with monitoring and review anomalies regularly. Apply **defense in depth** and least privilege to reduce potential blast radius.

risk_details: Without **Insights**, abnormal API call or error rates can go unnoticed, delaying detection of credential abuse, privilege escalation, or runaway automation. Attackers may rapidly alter policies, delete resources, or exfiltrate data before response, impacting confidentiality and availability.

message: Multiregion trail cloud-trail-grp01 has encryption disabled.
status_detail: Multiregion trail cloud-trail-grp01 has encryption disabled.

analytic.name: CloudTrail trail logs are encrypted at rest with a KMS key

finding_info.desc: **AWS CloudTrail trails** are evaluated for use of **SSE-KMS** with a customer-managed KMS key to encrypt delivered log files at rest in S3. Trails without a configured KMS key are identified. *Applies to single-Region and multi-Region trails.*
finding_info.title: CloudTrail trail logs are encrypted at rest with a KMS key
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark

remediation.desc: Enable **SSE-KMS** on every trail using a **customer-managed KMS key**. Apply **least privilege** so only authorized roles can `Decrypt`, and enforce **separation of duties** between key admins and log readers. Rotate keys and monitor key usage to provide **defense in depth** for CloudTrail data.

risk_details: Absent a **customer-managed KMS key**, log protection relies only on storage permissions. Bucket misconfigurations or stolen credentials can expose audit data, aiding evasion and lateral movement. Missing key-level controls, rotation, and usage audit weaken **confidentiality** and **forensic integrity**.

message: Multiregion trail cloud-trail-grp01 has log file validation enabled.
status_detail: Multiregion trail cloud-trail-grp01 has log file validation enabled.

analytic.name: CloudTrail trail has log file validation enabled

finding_info.desc:
**AWS CloudTrail trails** are evaluated for **log file integrity validation** being enabled (`LogFileValidationEnabled`).

When enabled, CloudTrail generates signed digest files to verify that S3-delivered log files remain unchanged.
finding_info.title: CloudTrail trail has log file validation enabled
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark

remediation.desc:
Enable **log file integrity validation** on all trails (`LogFileValidationEnabled=true`).

Enforce **least privilege** on the logs bucket, retain and protect digest files (e.g., S3 Object Lock/MFA Delete), and monitor validation results to support **defense in depth**.

risk_details:
Without validation, adversaries can alter, forge, or delete audit entries without detection, compromising log **integrity** and non-repudiation.

This impairs investigations, enables alert evasion, and obscures unauthorized changes across regions or accounts.

message: Multiregion Trail cloud-trail-grp01 S3 bucket access logging is not enabled for bucket cloud-trail-logs-grp01.
status_detail: Multiregion Trail cloud-trail-grp01 S3 bucket access logging is not enabled for bucket cloud-trail-logs-grp01.

AWS-Account-Security-Onboarding: Send S3 access logs for critical buckets to separate S3 bucket
Confirm that logs are present in S3 bucket and SIEM

analytic.name: CloudTrail trail destination S3 bucket has access logging enabled

finding_info.desc:
CloudTrail trails deliver logs to an S3 bucket; this evaluates whether that bucket has **S3 server access logging** enabled to record requests against it.

*If the destination bucket is outside the account or audit scope, a manual review is indicated.*
finding_info.title: CloudTrail trail destination S3 bucket has access logging enabled
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark

remediation.desc: Enable **S3 server access logging** on the CloudTrail logs bucket and write logs to a separate, tightly controlled bucket. Apply **least privilege**, enable **versioning**, and consider **Object Lock** to deter tampering. Centralize monitoring to support defense-in-depth and rapid investigation.

risk_details: Without access logging on the CloudTrail logs bucket, access and changes to log files lack an independent audit trail. Attackers could read, delete, or replace logs without attribution, undermining **log confidentiality** and **integrity**, and slowing **incident response**.

message: S3 Bucket cloud-trail-logs-grp01 from multiregion trail cloud-trail-grp01 is not publicly accessible.
status_detail: S3 Bucket cloud-trail-logs-grp01 from multiregion trail cloud-trail-grp01 is not publicly accessible.

analytic.name: CloudTrail trail S3 bucket is not publicly accessible

finding_info.desc:
CloudTrail log destination **S3 buckets** are inspected for ACL grants that expose data to the public `AllUsers` group.

Buckets hosted in other accounts are flagged for out-of-scope review.
finding_info.title: CloudTrail trail S3 bucket is not publicly accessible
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Network Reachability
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark
Effects/Data Exposure

remediation.desc:
Apply **least privilege** to the log bucket:
- Enable S3 `Block Public Access` (account and bucket)
- Remove `AllUsers`/`AuthenticatedUsers` ACLs; avoid wildcard principals
- Permit only CloudTrail and constrain with `aws:SourceArn`

Use a dedicated private bucket and monitor for permission changes.

risk_details:
Exposed CloudTrail logs erode **confidentiality** and **integrity**.

Adversaries can harvest API activity to map accounts, roles, and keys, enabling **reconnaissance** and evasion. If write is allowed, logs can be **poisoned** or deleted, thwarting investigations and compromising incident timelines.

status_detail: Trail cloud-trail-grp01 is multiregion and it is logging.

AWS-Account-Security-Onboarding: Enable as part of Organization trail

analytic.name: Region has at least one CloudTrail trail logging

finding_info.desc: **AWS CloudTrail** has at least one trail with `logging` enabled in every region. A **multi-region trail** or a regional trail counts for coverage in that region.
finding_info.title: Region has at least one CloudTrail trail logging
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark

remediation.desc:
Use a **multi-region CloudTrail trail** or per-region trails so `logging` is active in every region, including unused ones.

Centralize logs, enforce **least privilege** to log stores, and add **defense-in-depth** with encryption, integrity validation, and retention. Continuously monitor trail health to catch gaps.

risk_details:
Missing coverage in any region creates **visibility gaps**.

Attackers can use lesser-monitored regions to run API actions, hide **unauthorized changes**, and exfiltrate data without audit trails, weakening **detective controls**, hindering **forensics**, and delaying response (confidentiality and integrity).

remediation.desc:
Enable a **multi-region CloudTrail** that logs **management events** for `read` and `write` in all regions.

risk_details:

Adversaries can operate in overlooked regions to create resources, modify permissions, or disable logging, undermining **integrity**, **confidentiality**, and incident response.

unmapped.notes: This check evaluates all CloudWatch Log Groups in scope. Log groups that inherit the account-level policy pass. For log groups whose own policy is activated, the policy document is retrieved via GetDataProtectionPolicy to confirm that it audits or de-identifies at least one data identifier; every other log group fails without that call.

analytic.name: CloudWatch Log Groups have a data protection policy configured

finding_info.desc: **CloudWatch log groups** are checked to ensure a **data protection policy** is configured to audit and mask sensitive data identifiers such as PII and credentials.
finding_info.title: CloudWatch Log Groups have a data protection policy configured
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Effects/Data Exposure
Sensitive Data Identifications/PII

remediation.desc: Attach a data protection policy to CloudWatch Log Groups that may contain sensitive data. Choose managed data identifiers matching the data types your applications can log, or create an account-level policy to cover all log groups.

risk_details: CloudWatch Logs encrypts log data at rest by default. Without a data protection policy, sensitive data such as PII or credentials remains unmasked. Anyone with logs:GetLogEvents or logs:FilterLogEvents can view unmasked sensitive values, widening exposure and leading to compliance violations under GDPR, HIPAA, and PCI DSS.

message: Log Group /aws/ecs/containerinsights/gridguard-aws-sandbox/performance does not have AWS KMS keys associated.
status_detail: Log Group /aws/ecs/containerinsights/gridguard-aws-sandbox/performance does not have AWS KMS keys associated.

analytic.name: CloudWatch log group is encrypted with an AWS KMS key

finding_info.desc: **CloudWatch log groups** are assessed for **at-rest encryption** by checking if an **AWS KMS key** is associated with the log group via `kmsKeyId`.
finding_info.title: CloudWatch log group is encrypted with an AWS KMS key
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Effects/Data Exposure

remediation.desc:
Associate each log group with a **customer-managed KMS key** via `kmsKeyId`.
- Enforce **least privilege** in key and IAM policies, granting `kms:Decrypt` only to required principals
- Enable rotation and monitor key usage
- Separate keys by app/tenant to support **defense in depth** and rapid revocation

risk_details:
Without a **customer-managed KMS key**, logs rely on service-managed encryption, limiting control and auditability.
- Confidentiality: weaker key-policy barriers against unauthorized reads
- Integrity/availability: no custom rotation or rapid revoke, hindering incident response and compliance

Reduce exposure: enforce **least privilege**, keep root for *break-glass* with MFA, disable root access keys, and route alerts into incident response for **defense in depth**.

risk_details:

- confidentiality via data access/exfiltration
- integrity via policy/config tampering
- availability via deletions or shutdowns
Delayed detection increases blast radius and persistence.

message: AMI Block Public Access is enabled in ap-northeast-1.
status_detail: AMI Block Public Access is enabled in ap-northeast-1.

analytic.name: AMI block public access is enabled at the account level

finding_info.desc: AMI block public access configuration is assessed to see whether public sharing of AMIs is blocked in the account and Region. When enabled (`block-new-sharing`), no AMI in the Region can be made public regardless of individual image permissions.
finding_info.title: AMI block public access is enabled at the account level
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Effects/Data Exposure

remediation.desc: Enable AMI block public access (`block-new-sharing`) in every active Region. Apply guardrails (SCPs) to prevent it from being disabled, and review any AMIs that are currently shared publicly.

risk_details: Without blocking public access, AMIs could be accidentally or maliciously shared publicly, exposing baked-in secrets, source code, and infrastructure details to unauthorized actors.

message: EBS Default Encryption is not activated.
status_detail: EBS Default Encryption is not activated.

analytic.name: EBS default encryption is enabled

finding_info.desc: **EBS** uses `encryption by default` at the account and region level, ensuring new volumes, snapshots, and AMI-backed volumes are automatically encrypted with a chosen **KMS key**
finding_info.title: EBS default encryption is enabled
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark
Effects/Data Exposure

remediation.desc: Enable `EBS encryption by default` in every region and select a **customer-managed KMS key**. Apply **least privilege** to key use, rotate keys, and monitor access. Enforce encrypted volume creation with organizational guardrails and secure templates as **defense in depth**.

risk_details: Without `encryption by default`, data on new **EBS volumes** and **snapshots** may be stored in plaintext. A compromised account or mis-shared snapshot can expose disk contents, enabling data exfiltration, offline analysis, and loss of **confidentiality**.

message: EBS Snapshot vol-0ee0864aed0b00a3d is unencrypted.
status_detail: EBS Snapshot vol-0ee0864aed0b00a3d is unencrypted.

analytic.name: EBS volume is encrypted

finding_info.desc:
**EBS volumes** are assessed for **encryption at rest** using **AWS KMS**.

The finding identifies volumes whose `encrypted` state is disabled, meaning data is stored unencrypted on block storage.
finding_info.title: EBS volume is encrypted
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark
Effects/Data Exposure

remediation.desc:
Encrypt all EBS volumes and enable `encryption by default` for new volumes and snapshot copies.

Apply **least privilege** to KMS keys, restrict snapshot sharing, and enforce **defense in depth** with policies and templates that prevent creation of unencrypted storage.

risk_details:
Unencrypted volumes or snapshots can be copied, shared, or recovered and reveal raw data, undermining **confidentiality**.

Adversaries with host or account access can read disks offline, harvest secrets, or alter system images, affecting **integrity** and enabling **lateral movement**.

message: EBS Volume vol-0ee0864aed0b00a3d is not protected by a backup plan.
status_detail: EBS Volume vol-0ee0864aed0b00a3d is not protected by a backup plan.

analytic.name: EBS volume is protected by a backup plan

finding_info.desc: **EBS volumes** are evaluated for coverage by an **AWS Backup plan**, whether explicitly targeted or included via broad resource selection, confirming scheduled, policy-driven backups exist for the volume.
finding_info.title: EBS volume is protected by a backup plan
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Effects/Data Destruction

remediation.desc: Include all critical EBS volumes in standardized **AWS Backup** plans aligned to your `RPO`/`RTO`. Use tags for automatic assignment, enable cross-Region/account copies, apply **Vault Lock** for WORM retention, encrypt with KMS, enforce least-privilege access, and regularly test restores to verify integrity.

risk_details: Absent backup coverage, volumes face **data loss**, weakened **integrity**, and reduced **availability**. Deletion or corruption-whether accidental or malicious-can leave no recovery path, causing prolonged outages, failed point-in-time restoration, unmet retention needs, and harder incident response.

message: Snapshots not found for the EBS volume vol-0ee0864aed0b00a3d.
status_detail: Snapshots not found for the EBS volume vol-0ee0864aed0b00a3d.

analytic.name: EBS volume has at least one snapshot

finding_info.desc: **EBS volumes** are evaluated for the existence of at least one associated **snapshot**, identifying volumes without any point-in-time backup available.
finding_info.title: EBS volume has at least one snapshot
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Effects/Data Destruction

remediation.desc:
Establish automated, policy-based **EBS snapshot** coverage for all volumes aligned to business `RPO/RTO`.
- Schedule regular snapshots with retention controls
- Encrypt snapshots and enforce **least privilege** access
- Replicate to another Region/account for DR
- Periodically test restores and document procedures

risk_details: Missing **EBS snapshots** removes point-in-time recovery. Accidental deletion, corruption, or ransomware can cause **irrecoverable data loss** and prolonged **service outages**, degrading data **integrity** and **availability** and complicating recovery and forensics.

message: IMDSv2 is not enabled by default for EC2 instances.
status_detail: IMDSv2 is not enabled by default for EC2 instances.

analytic.name: IMDSv2 is required by default for EC2 instances at the account level

finding_info.desc: **EC2 account IMDS defaults** with `http_tokens`=`required` ensure new instances in the Region use **IMDSv2** by default and disable IMDSv1. *Existing instances keep their current setting.*
finding_info.title: IMDSv2 is required by default for EC2 instances at the account level
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
TTPs/Credential Access

remediation.desc: Enforce **IMDSv2** at the account level in every Region by setting `http_tokens` to `required`. Add guardrails with **SCP/IAM conditions**. Standardize AMIs and launch templates to require tokens, validate workload compatibility, and apply **least privilege** to instance roles for defense in depth. *For containers*, prefer hop limit `2`.

risk_details: Without a default of **IMDSv2**, new instances may enable **IMDSv1**, exposing metadata via simple HTTP. SSRF or proxy misconfigs can steal **temporary IAM credentials**, enabling data exfiltration (confidentiality), unauthorized API changes (integrity), and lateral movement that can disrupt services (availability).

message: EC2 Instance i-0e9c059268937f103 does not have detailed monitoring enabled.
status_detail: EC2 Instance i-0e9c059268937f103 does not have detailed monitoring enabled.

analytic.name: EC2 instance has detailed monitoring enabled

finding_info.desc:
**EC2 instances** are assessed for **CloudWatch detailed monitoring**, indicating whether 1-minute metrics collection is enabled.

Instances lacking this setting provide only 5-minute metrics.
finding_info.title: EC2 instance has detailed monitoring enabled
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices

remediation.desc: Enable **detailed monitoring** to collect `1-minute` metrics on critical instances. Use **defense in depth**: baseline normal behavior, create alerts for anomalies, and correlate metrics with logs and traces. Review dashboards regularly. *If costs matter*, prioritize production, internet-facing, and autoscaling fleets.

risk_details:
Without 1-minute metrics, visibility drops, delaying detection of:
- Sudden CPU/network/disk spikes affecting **availability**
- **Malicious workloads** (crypto-mining, brute force)
- **Data exfiltration** patterns
Slower detection expands blast radius, raising incident impact and response cost.

message: EC2 Instance i-0e9c059268937f103 has IMDSv2 enabled and required.
status_detail: EC2 Instance i-0e9c059268937f103 has IMDSv2 enabled and required.

analytic.name: EC2 instance requires IMDSv2 or has the instance metadata service disabled

finding_info.desc: **EC2 instances** are evaluated for **IMDSv2 enforcement**: metadata endpoint enabled with `http_tokens: required`, or metadata service fully disabled (`http_endpoint: disabled`).
finding_info.title: EC2 instance requires IMDSv2 or has the instance metadata service disabled
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark
TTPs/Credential Access

remediation.desc:
Apply defense in depth:
- Require **IMDSv2** tokens on all instances (`http_tokens: required`)
- Disable metadata where not needed (`http_endpoint: disabled`)
- Minimize hop limit to `1` when feasible
- Update SDKs/apps for IMDSv2
- Restrict instance profile permissions (least privilege)
- Block metadata access from untrusted workloads

risk_details: Permitting **IMDSv1** or optional tokens lets SSRF or compromised workloads retrieve **temporary IAM credentials**, impacting confidentiality and integrity. Stolen role creds can drive **privilege escalation**, unauthorized data access, and lateral movement across AWS resources.

message: EC2 Instance i-0e9c059268937f103 is not internet facing with an instance profile.
status_detail: EC2 Instance i-0e9c059268937f103 is not internet facing with an instance profile.

analytic.name: EC2 instance is not internet-facing with an instance profile attached

finding_info.desc:
**EC2 instances** with a public IP address and an attached **instance profile** (IAM role) are identified.

Instances lacking public exposure or without an instance profile are excluded.
finding_info.title: EC2 instance is not internet-facing with an instance profile attached
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Network Reachability
TTPs/Initial Access
TTPs/Credential Access

remediation.desc: Avoid direct Internet exposure. Place workloads behind an **Application Load Balancer** and protect HTTP apps with **WAF**. Remove public IPs or restrict ingress to trusted sources. Apply **least privilege** to instance profiles and enforce **IMDSv2**. Use **bastion hosts** or **Session Manager** for admin access.

risk_details: Publicly reachable instances with **IAM role credentials** expand the blast radius. Remote exploits or misconfigurations can steal credentials via the **instance metadata service**, enabling unauthorized API calls, data exfiltration, and lateral movement, impacting confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

message: EC2 Instance i-0e9c059268937f103 is unmanaged by Systems Manager because it is stopped.
status_detail: EC2 Instance i-0e9c059268937f103 is unmanaged by Systems Manager because it is stopped.

analytic.name: EC2 instance is managed by AWS Systems Manager or not running

finding_info.desc: **EC2 instances** are assessed for enrollment as **Systems Manager managed nodes**. Running instances lacking Systems Manager registration are marked as unmanaged; instances in `stopped`, `terminated`, or `pending` states are noted separately.
finding_info.title: EC2 instance is managed by AWS Systems Manager or not running
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Patch Management

remediation.desc: Enroll all instances as **Systems Manager managed nodes**. Prefer **Session Manager** over SSH/RDP, restrict inbound admin ports, and use **least privilege** roles. Ensure connectivity to SSM endpoints (or private endpoints), automate patching and inventory, and monitor activity for defense-in-depth.

risk_details: Unmanaged instances lack centralized patching, inventory, and secure remote access. This increases exposure to brute force on SSH/RDP, delayed patching, and poor visibility. Exploits can enable lateral movement and persistence, degrading confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

message: EC2 Instance i-0e9c059268937f103 is not running.
status_detail: EC2 Instance i-0e9c059268937f103 is not running.

analytic.name: EC2 instance is not older than the configured maximum age or is not running

finding_info.desc: **EC2 instances** are evaluated for age while in `running` state. Instances launched beyond the configurable limit (`max_ec2_instance_age_in_days`, default `180`) are flagged as older than the allowed lifetime. Stopped instances are ignored.
finding_info.title: EC2 instance is not older than the configured maximum age or is not running
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Patch Management

remediation.desc:
Adopt **short-lived, patched workloads**:
- Rebuild regularly from hardened, updated images; rotate AMIs
- Use centralized patch management and vulnerability scanning
- Retire or modernize legacy hosts; tag for lifecycle
- Apply **least privilege** and **defense in depth** to limit blast radius

Adjust `max_ec2_instance_age_in_days` to match policy.

risk_details:
Long-lived instances often run **unpatched OS and agents**, enabling:
- Exploitation of known CVEs  loss of confidentiality
- Privilege escalation and tampering  integrity compromise
- Malware/crypto-mining and instability  reduced availability

Aged hosts also drift from baselines and impede response.

message: EC2 Instance i-0e9c059268937f103 virtualization type is set to HVM.
status_detail: EC2 Instance i-0e9c059268937f103 virtualization type is set to HVM.

analytic.name: EC2 instance virtualization type is HVM

finding_info.desc: **EC2 instances** are evaluated for their virtualization mode. Instances with `virtualization_type` set to `paravirtual` are identified; those using **HVM** are recognized as hardware-assisted virtualization.
finding_info.title: EC2 instance virtualization type is HVM
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices

remediation.desc: Standardize on **HVM/Nitro**. Migrate PV workloads to HVM AMIs and current instance families; ensure support for `ENA` and `NVMe`, current kernels, and hardened configs. Apply **defense in depth** and **least privilege**. Use immutable images with staged testing, then retire PV images to prevent drift and regressions.

risk_details: Using **paravirtual (PV)** weakens isolation versus **HVM/Nitro** and blocks features like `ENA` and `NVMe`. Confidentiality and integrity can suffer due to reliance on legacy hypercalls/drivers; availability and performance may degrade under load, increasing exposure to kernel/driver exploits and noisy-neighbor impacts.

message: Instance i-0e9c059268937f103 does not have Cassandra ports open to the Internet.
status_detail: Instance i-0e9c059268937f103 does not have Cassandra ports open to the Internet.

analytic.name: EC2 instance does not have Cassandra ports (TCP 7000, 7001, 7199, 9042, 9160) open to the Internet

finding_info.desc:
**EC2 instances** have **Cassandra service ports** (`7000`, `7001`, `7199`, `9042`, `9160`) reachable from the Internet through security group ingress.

Public IP presence and subnet exposure are considered to assess external reachability.
finding_info.title: EC2 instance does not have Cassandra ports (TCP 7000, 7001, 7199, 9042, 9160) open to the Internet
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Network Reachability
TTPs/Initial Access
Effects/Data Exposure

remediation.desc:
Apply **least privilege network access**:
- Remove `0.0.0.0/0` and `::/0` to Cassandra ports
- Allow only trusted subnets or VPN/bastion
- Keep nodes in private subnets; segment inter-node traffic
- Enforce **authentication** and **TLS/mTLS** for clients and JMX
- Add **defense in depth** with NACLs and monitoring

risk_details:
Internet-exposed Cassandra enables unauthorized queries on `9042`, remote management via `7199` (JMX), and tampering with inter-node channels on `7000/7001` and `9160`.

Attackers can read/modify data (**confidentiality, integrity**), disrupt or take over the cluster (**availability**), and pivot within the VPC.

message: Instance i-0e9c059268937f103 does not have CIFS ports open to the Internet.
status_detail: Instance i-0e9c059268937f103 does not have CIFS ports open to the Internet.

analytic.name: EC2 instance does not allow Internet ingress to TCP ports 139 or 445 (CIFS)

finding_info.desc:
**EC2 instances** with security groups permitting **inbound** TCP `139` or `445` (**CIFS/SMB**) from `0.0.0.0/0` are identified.

Exposure level reflects whether the instance has a **public IP** and the subnet's Internet reachability.
finding_info.title: EC2 instance does not allow Internet ingress to TCP ports 139 or 445 (CIFS)
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Network Reachability
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
TTPs/Initial Access
Effects/Data Exposure

remediation.desc:
Restrict **CIFS/SMB** to trusted internal sources using **least privilege**; do not allow `0.0.0.0/0`.

Adopt **defense in depth**: place hosts in private subnets, require **VPN** or controlled jump paths, and enforce **segmentation**. Disable SMB if unnecessary or use alternatives (e.g., SFTP). Require strong auth and SMB signing.

risk_details: Publicly reachable **SMB** allows unauthorized access and **remote code execution**, enabling credential theft, NTLM relay, and share enumeration. Attackers can exfiltrate files, tamper or delete data, and spread **ransomware**, degrading **confidentiality**, **integrity**, and **availability**.

message: Instance i-0e9c059268937f103 does not have Elasticsearch/Kibana ports open to the Internet.
status_detail: Instance i-0e9c059268937f103 does not have Elasticsearch/Kibana ports open to the Internet.

analytic.name: EC2 instance does not allow ingress from the Internet to Elasticsearch and Kibana ports (TCP 9200, 9300, 5601)

finding_info.desc:
**EC2 instances** with **Elasticsearch/Kibana ports** (`9200`, `9300`, `5601`) exposed to the Internet through inbound security group rules.

Assesses reachability considering instance public IP and subnet to reflect real exposure.
finding_info.title: EC2 instance does not allow ingress from the Internet to Elasticsearch and Kibana ports (TCP 9200, 9300, 5601)
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Network Reachability
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
TTPs/Initial Access/Unauthorized Access
Effects/Data Exposure

remediation.desc:
Apply **least privilege** to network exposure:
- Restrict `9200`, `9300`, `5601` to trusted sources or keep them private
- Use **private subnets**, **VPN/peering**, or **bastion/SSM** for admin access
- Enforce **authentication** and **TLS** on Elasticsearch/Kibana
- Avoid public IPs unless strictly required

risk_details:
Public access to Elasticsearch/Kibana can lead to:
- Unauthorized queries or dashboard viewing  confidentiality loss
- Index changes or cluster control via `9300`  integrity impact
- Scans and bulk queries  availability degradation

Enables data exfiltration and lateral movement.

message: Instance i-0e9c059268937f103 does not have FTP ports open to the Internet.
status_detail: Instance i-0e9c059268937f103 does not have FTP ports open to the Internet.

analytic.name: EC2 instance does not allow ingress from the Internet to TCP ports 20 or 21 (FTP)

finding_info.desc:
**EC2 instances** with security groups permitting inbound **FTP** on `TCP 20-21` from any address (e.g., `0.0.0.0/0` or `::/0`) are identified.

Exposure is contextualized by the instance's public reachability (public IP and subnet).
finding_info.title: EC2 instance does not allow ingress from the Internet to TCP ports 20 or 21 (FTP)
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Network Reachability
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
TTPs/Initial Access
Effects/Data Exposure

remediation.desc: Deny public ingress to **FTP** ports `20-21` following **least privilege**. Prefer **SFTP** or **FTPS**; if transfers are required, restrict to trusted sources and use private access (VPN or dedicated network). Apply **defense in depth** with tightened security groups and network ACLs, and monitor authentication and access.

risk_details:
Exposed **FTP** invites Internet brute force and transmits in cleartext, enabling credential theft and packet sniffing (**confidentiality**).

Attackers can upload/alter files (**integrity**) and abuse services for malware staging or DoS (**availability**). Publicly reachable hosts are rapidly probed by scanners.

message: Instance i-0e9c059268937f103 does not have Kafka port 9092 open to the Internet.
status_detail: Instance i-0e9c059268937f103 does not have Kafka port 9092 open to the Internet.

analytic.name: EC2 instance does not allow ingress from the Internet to TCP port 9092 (Kafka)

finding_info.desc: **EC2 instances** with security group rules that allow inbound `TCP 9092` (Kafka) from the Internet are reported. The evaluation inspects ingress rules to detect broad sources (for example `0.0.0.0/0` or `::/0`) that expose Kafka brokers.
finding_info.title: EC2 instance does not allow ingress from the Internet to TCP port 9092 (Kafka)
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Network Reachability

TTPs/Initial Access

remediation.desc: Apply **least privilege**: restrict `TCP 9092` to trusted networks, not `0.0.0.0/0` or `::/0`. Keep brokers in private subnets and use private connectivity (VPN/peering). risk_details: Public Kafka access undermines CIA: adversaries can read topics and metadata (**confidentiality**), publish or alter events (**integrity**), and overwhelm brokers (**availability**). Exposure also eases reconnaissance and lateral movement from the broker host.

message: Instance i-0e9c059268937f103 does not have Kerberos ports open to the Internet.
status_detail: Instance i-0e9c059268937f103 does not have Kerberos ports open to the Internet.

analytic.name: EC2 instance does not allow ingress from the Internet to TCP ports 88, 464, 749, or 750 (Kerberos)

finding_info.desc:
**EC2 instances** whose security groups allow public **inbound TCP** access to Kerberos ports `88`, `464`, `749`, or `750` (authentication, password change, admin).

Rules permitting `0.0.0.0/0` or `::/0` are treated as Internet-exposed.
finding_info.title: EC2 instance does not allow ingress from the Internet to TCP ports 88, 464, 749, or 750 (Kerberos)
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Network Reachability
TTPs/Initial Access/Unauthorized Access

remediation.desc:
Restrict Kerberos ports to trusted sources only.
- Prefer **private connectivity** (VPN, peering) over public exposure
- Place KDCs/services in private subnets without public IPs
- Apply **least privilege** with narrowly scoped security group rules and NACLs
- Add defense-in-depth: host firewalls and monitor authentication activity

risk_details:
Public Kerberos exposure risks CIA:
- **Password spraying**/AS-REP roasting against accounts
- Unauthorized password changes on `464`
- Realm/user enumeration and DoS of KDC/services

Stolen tickets enable **lateral movement** and privilege escalation in Active Directory or the Kerberos realm.

finding_info.desc:

Public exposure context (presence of public IP and subnet reachability) is considered to gauge how broadly these ports can be accessed.
finding_info.title: EC2 instance does not allow ingress from the Internet to TCP ports 389 or 636 (LDAP/LDAPS)
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Network Reachability
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
TTPs/Initial Access/Unauthorized Access

remediation.desc:
Limit LDAP to trusted networks:
- Allowlist specific source CIDRs in security groups (*least privilege*)
- Use **private connectivity** (peering/VPN) instead of Internet
- Require **LDAPS**, strong certificates, and disable insecure binds
- Add NACLs and monitoring for defense in depth

risk_details:
Publicly reachable **LDAP/LDAPS** enables:

- **Password spraying** and credential theft (cleartext on `389`)
- Unauthorized queries causing **data exfiltration**

Abuse may lead to **privilege escalation** and availability impact via account lockouts.

message: EC2 Instance i-0e9c059268937f103 not associated with an Instance Profile Role.
status_detail: EC2 Instance i-0e9c059268937f103 not associated with an Instance Profile Role.

analytic.name: EC2 instance is associated with an IAM instance profile role

finding_info.desc: **EC2 instances** are evaluated for association with an **IAM instance profile role** that delivers temporary credentials to workloads running on the instance
finding_info.title: EC2 instance is associated with an IAM instance profile role
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark

remediation.desc: Attach an **IAM instance profile** to every instance and grant only permissions each workload requires (**least privilege**). Eliminate static keys on hosts; use **temporary credentials** with automatic rotation. Separate roles per application, enforce **separation of duties**, and limit who can assign roles (govern via `iam:PassRole`). Monitor role usage for anomalies.

risk_details: Without an instance profile, apps often rely on long-term access keys on the host. Exposed keys can be used from anywhere to read data, alter resources, or disrupt services, impacting confidentiality, integrity, and availability. Keys may persist in AMIs, images, or logs, hindering rotation and amplifying blast radius.

risk_details: Publicly addressed instances are Internet-scannable, enabling direct probing and brute-force of exposed services and management ports. This increases risks of unauthorized access, remote code execution, and data exfiltration (**confidentiality, integrity**), and allows direct DDoS targeting, degrading **availability**.

remediation.desc: Avoid placing secrets in User Data. Store them in a **managed secret service** and fetch at runtime via a **least-privilege instance role**. risk_details: **Secrets embedded in User Data** undermine confidentiality and integrity. Anyone with instance or build-system access can read them, reuse credentials to call services, exfiltrate data, or move laterally. Exposure may persist in AMIs, snapshots, and backups, increasing blast radius over time.

message: EC2 Instance i-0e9c059268937f103 has been stopped longer than 30 days (45 days).
status_detail: EC2 Instance i-0e9c059268937f103 has been stopped longer than 30 days (45 days).

analytic.name: EC2 instance has not been stopped longer than the configured maximum days

finding_info.desc: **EC2 instances** in the `stopped` state are evaluated for how long they have remained stopped. Instances stopped beyond the configurable limit (`max_ec2_instance_stopped_days`, default `30`) are flagged. Running, pending, and other non-stopped instances pass.
finding_info.title: EC2 instance has not been stopped longer than the configured maximum days
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Patch Management

remediation.desc:
Establish a lifecycle policy for stopped instances:
- Tag instances with owner and expiry
- Terminate instances no longer needed to reclaim EBS cost
- If retained, start regularly for patching or rebuild from a hardened AMI
- Prefer ephemeral, autoscaled workloads over long-lived stopped hosts

Adjust `max_ec2_instance_stopped_days` to match policy.

risk_details: Long-stopped instances remain **unmonitored and unpatched** while still retaining EBS volumes, network configuration, IAM instance profiles, and SSH keys. This expands attack surface and incurs unnecessary storage cost. Stale AMIs and credentials attached to abandoned instances increase the chance of compromise if the instance is later started.

message: EC2 Instance i-0e9c059268937f103 uses only one ENI: ( Interfaces: ['eni-08500fb2c9211b421'] ).
status_detail: EC2 Instance i-0e9c059268937f103 uses only one ENI: ( Interfaces: ['eni-08500fb2c9211b421'] ).

analytic.name: EC2 instance has no more than one Elastic Network Interface (ENI) attached

finding_info.desc: **EC2 instances** are evaluated for attached network adapters. It identifies instances with more than one `ENI`-including `efa`, `interface`, or `trunk` types-and distinguishes those using a single adapter.
finding_info.title: EC2 instance has no more than one Elastic Network Interface (ENI) attached
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Network Reachability

remediation.desc:
Prefer a **single ENI per instance**.

If multi-homing is unavoidable:
- Place ENIs in least-privilege subnets/SGs
- Keep `source/destination check` enabled and routes explicit
- Use gateways/LBs for NAT or ingress, not the host
- Monitor flow logs and formally approve exceptions

Embed **defense in depth** and **zero trust**.

risk_details: **Multiple ENIs** create dual-homed hosts across subnets and security groups, enabling unintended routing and policy bypass. Adversaries can pivot between segments, use alternate egress for **data exfiltration**, or exploit asymmetric paths, undermining segmentation and **confidentiality/integrity** while complicating containment.

remediation.desc: Adopt **non-deprecated, maintained AMIs** and perform rolling replacements of affected instances. Standardize on hardened golden images with **regular AMI rotation** and `DeprecationTime` monitoring. Update launch templates/ASGs to reference current images.
